title: Reachability through an out-of-range length query
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural number, $l,l_1,l_0$ machine labels, $st$ a seven-register state, and $c$ an abstract machine configuration. Suppose the instruction at $l$ queries whether the whole input length exceeds the pointer register, with $l_1$ the positive-answer label and $l_0$ the negative-answer label. If every register of $st$ is at most $B$, the pointer value in $st$ is at least $|x|$, and there is a run from label $l_0$ with register values given by $st$ to $c$, with the guard satisfied at every earlier step, then there is such a guarded run from label $l$ with the same register values to $c$.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $l$ is a whole-input query to the input-length decider using the pointer register, with branches $l_1$ and $l_0$
Every register of $st$ is at most $B$
The pointer value in $st$ is not less than $|x|$
There is a guarded run from $(l_0,st)$ to $c$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural-number register bound,
$\ell,\ell_1,\ell_0$ machine labels, $t$ a machine state, and $c$ a machine
configuration. If the instruction at $\ell$ is a whole-input query to the input-length
decider using the pointer register, every register of $t$ is at most $B$, the pointer
value in $t$ is not less than $|x|$, and there is a guarded run from label $\ell_0$ with
state $t$ to $c$, then there is such a guarded run from label $\ell$ with state $t$ to
$c$.
